steps.say: A cohesive text flows smoothly from one idea to the next.
Start each paragraph with a topic sentence that tells the reader what it is about.
Use connectives to show how ideas link.
Use pronouns and synonyms to avoid repeating a noun, but make sure the reader knows who or what they mean.
Every sentence in a paragraph should be about the same topic.

hints: A contrast shows a different or opposite idea.
Think about which connective you would use to give the other side.
Try each connective before: some people disagree.
check.explanation: On the other hand introduces a contrasting idea.

check.prompt: Write one pronoun to replace the second Pak Rudi. Pak Rudi is our football coach. Pak Rudi trains us every Tuesday.
hints: A pronoun can stand for a person who has already been named.
Which pronoun is used for a man?
check.explanation: He replaces Pak Rudi in the second sentence, so the name is not repeated.
